Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows a focal opacity in the right lower lung, to the follow-up image (Figure 4), there is a clear increase in the density and extent of the right-sided opacity along with the development of new opacities in the left lung. This pattern of progressive, multifocal airspace disease without cavitation or rapid resolution is most consistent with the description of adenocarcinoma in situ (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma) among the given choices.
